reasoning: The retrieved fragments partially overlap with the obligation in Article 15(5) but do not fully implement it. ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 section 5 (Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment) requires assessment of data sources and data quality and documenting known model limitations, which is relevant to the underlying topics of data integrity and model flaws. ACME-POL-MRM-003 section 1 (Model Risk Management Standard) establishes requirements to identify, assess, and manage model risk across AI models, which also maps to the general obligation to manage risks to models. However, none of the fragments explicitly require the technical cybersecurity measures the regulation mandates: there is no explicit requirement for measures to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve or control attacks that manipulate training data (data poisoning), inputs that cause model mistakes (adversarial examples), or to remediate model flaws. Missing elements include explicit technical controls (e.g., data poisoning prevention, adversarial robustness testing, input sanitization/validation, runtime anomaly detection, incident response procedures for adversarial attacks, patching/remediation processes), explicit coverage of "where appropriate" cybersecurity measures for high‑risk AI, and operationalization (tooling, monitoring metrics, testing procedures) of those controls. Because these policy fragments address the same subject area (data quality and model risk) but omit the specific cybersecurity/technical measures and incident response capabilities required by Article 15(5), this is a potential impact that warrants human Compliance Analyst review and policy remediation.

citations.internal: ACME-POL-AIGOV-002, 5. Risk Assessment Prior to Deployment

retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Before any AI system is deployed to production, the owning business unit must
complete a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment covering:

- Intended purpose and use cases
- Data sources and data quality
- Known limitations of the model or system
- Fairness and bias considerations
- Sign-off from the AIGC for high-impact systems

retrieved_fragments.policy_title: Acme Bank Model Risk Management Standard
retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
This Standard sets out the requirements for identifying, assessing, and managing
model risk across all quantitative models used by Acme Bank, including statistical,
machine learning, and AI-based models.

Applies to all AI systems used in production, including those developed in-house
and those procured from third parties, across all business lines.
